title: Fix a failure on a NWChem test reported in #1806
body:
Related to #1806

# Short summary

This MR fixes the failure on a NWChem test reported in #1806.

Shortly, this failure may be triggered by the bug fix between NWChem 7.0.0 and NWChem 7.2.3 when setting a periodic system together with a Gaussian basis set. This MR fixes this by changing `theory` in the `NWChem` calculator to `pspw` (pseudo-potential plane-wave) as well as the reference force-constant value.

As found in the [pipeline](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/jobs/11957844818), the NWChem failure has been solved in this MR. There is still a remaining octopus failure, which may be addressed in a separate MR.

@askhl: Maybe this MR can be merged rather quickly. Could you have a look when you have a short time?

# A bit detailed survey

As stated in #1806, the failure happened between the following two pipelines.
- https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/pipelines/2048489285 (passed: nwchem 7.0.0, python 3.12.11)
- https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/pipelines/2050944500 (failed: nwchem 7.2.3, python 3.13.7)

By running the test code for H2 (consistent with the failed test), I obtained the following NWChem output:
```
                                 NWChem DFT Module
                                 -----------------


                                      nwchem


 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
 dft_rdinput: detected periodicity =                    3
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  current input line :
    30: task dft energy
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
 There is an error in the input file
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
 For more information see the NWChem manual at https://nwchemgit.github.io


 For further details see manual section:
0:dft_rdinput: detected periodicity =:Received an Error in Communication
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
MPI_ABORT was invoked on rank 0 in communicator MPI COMM 3 DUP FROM 0
  Proc: [[26570,0],0]
  Errorcode: 3

NOTE: invoking MPI_ABORT causes Open MPI to kill all MPI processes.
You may or may not see output from other processes, depending on
exactly when Open MPI kills them.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
As found, the failure is related to the periodicity of the system.
Indeed, there is [a bug report in NWChem GitHub repo](
https://github.com/nwchemgit/nwchem/issues/322) (2021-02-12); NWChem cannot compute a periodic system with a Gaussian basis set, but before there was no error raised. This was fixed at that time.
This fix has been introduced between [NWChem 7.0.0 released on 2020-02-26](https://github.com/nwchemgit/nwchem/releases/tag/v7.0.0-release) and [NWChem 7.2.3 released on 2024-08-28](https://github.com/nwchemgit/nwchem/releases/tag/v7.2.3-release).

Regarding ASE `NWChem` calculator, [it sets a Gaussian basis set by default](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.26.0/ase/io/nwchem/nwwriter.py?ref_type=tags#L111), while [the failed test considers H2 in a periodic cell](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.26.0/ase/test/calculator/test_h2_bond_force.py?ref_type=tags#L13-14).
Before (NWChem 7.0.0), I guess the periodicity may be simply ignored in NWChem, while later (NWChem 7.2.3), this gets detected as an error in NWChem, which probably caused the failure of the test.
